reason: Substance holds: re-opened packet.js quran 3 --verse 2.190; under his own 2:190 heading al-Tabari prefers the view of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (not repealed, claiming repeal without proof is arbitrary), then paraphrases the ayah in his own voice: God commanded them to fight those who do fight, of the fighting men of the people of unbelief (muqatilat ahl al-kufr), not their women and children; and glosses wa-la taʿtadu as not killing a child, a woman, or any who have given the jizya of the two Books and the Magians. All three evidence runs re-found verbatim. verse.js ok (Al-Baqarah 2:190, at 196). Plain sense matches 2:190 to 2:193. But the revision introduced a watch-list term: entry-check warns that ‘unbelievers’ is on the quran watch list, and rule 4 says other groups are named only as the day’s text names them. The day’s text names this very group in the next ayah, 2:191, as ‘disbelievers’ (‘Such is the reward of disbelievers’), and Pickthall never writes ‘unbelievers’ anywhere in day 3. The reviser’s reason does not address the warning. A one-word fix clears it at the same length.
better: Replace ‘the unbelievers’ fighting men’ with ‘the disbelievers’ fighting men’ (Pickthall’s word in 2:191): ‘The verse opens the ayahs commanding the believers to fight, slay and drive out those who fight them; al-Tabari, on 2:190, takes it as unrepealed, binding against the disbelievers’ fighting men, and reads the forbidden aggression as killing women, children or those who pay tribute.’ Tested: entry-check.js ok, no warns (scratch/rr2-d003-fix.json).
